tools.name: check_text
tools.description: Decide whether one text should be allowed: profanity, slurs, insults, threats and sexual language, disguised spellings included (sh1t, f.u.c.k, leetspeak, homoglyphs). Returns the action (allow, review, block), the matches with their categories and the tricks used, a one-sentence reason and a censor

tools.name: check_batch
tools.description: Check up to 100 texts in one call, 30,000 characters in all, with the same settings. Each item has your id and a text; results come back in order, each with its id and either a result (as check_text returns) or an error. Read-only; counts one check per item.

tools.name: report_result
tools.description: Tell Unprofane a check got it wrong (or right): the result's id, the verdict and, if you know it, the action it should have taken. A person reads every report and corrections ship in a later engine. Writes a report; it changes no result and counts no check.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: The checks this key's account has used in the current billing period, how many its plan includes and any overage, with the share answered by the rules alone, the model or the cache. Counts up to the last full hour. Read-only and free.

tools.name: get_integration_snippet
tools.description: A complete, runnable recipe for adding Unprofane to a platform in a language: code to paste. Use it when asked to add a profanity or username filter to an app. Read-only and free: it checks no text.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "check_text" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: text, context, policy, mode, language, country, mask

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "check_batch" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: items, context, policy, mode, language, country, mask

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_text · Public sink: get_usage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_text · Public sink: get_usage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_text" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
